title: Count Beautiful Splits in an Array
statement:
You are given an integer array `nums` of length `n`. A **split** cuts the array into three non-empty contiguous parts `A`, `B`, `C` (so `A + B + C = nums`, where `+` means concatenation, and every element belongs to exactly one part).

A split is **beautiful** if at least one of the following holds:

- `A` is a prefix of `B`: `B` starts with exactly the elements of `A` (so `B` is at least as long as `A`).
- `B` is a prefix of `C`: `C` starts with exactly the elements of `B` (so `C` is at least as long as `B`).

Two splits are different if they cut the array at different positions. Count the beautiful splits. A split that satisfies both conditions is counted once.
inputFormat: The first line contains `n`. The second line contains the `n` integers of `nums`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of beautiful splits.

examples.explanation: The beautiful splits (A | B | C) are: [1] | [1] | [2,1,1,2], [1] | [1,2] | [1,1,2], [1] | [1,2,1] | [1,2], [1] | [1,2,1,1] | [2] (in all four, A = [1] is a prefix of B), and [1,1,2] | [1] | [1,2] (B = [1] is a prefix of C). Every other split fails both conditions.
There are three splits: [5] | [5] | [5,5] and [5] | [5,5] | [5] (A is a prefix of B), and [5,5] | [5] | [5] (B is a prefix of C). All three are beautiful.
The only split is [1] | [2] | [3]. A is not a prefix of B and B is not a prefix of C.

hints: A split is determined by two cut positions `i < j`. Checking a split by comparing elements directly costs O(n), giving O(n^3) overall. You need an O(1) check per split.

`A` is a prefix of `B` exactly when `B` is long enough (`j - i >= i`) and the suffix starting at `i` has a common prefix of length at least `i` with the whole array. One Z-function of `nums` answers this for every `i`.

`B` is a prefix of `C` when the suffixes starting at `i` and at `j` share a common prefix of length at least `j - i`. For each `i`, the Z-function of the suffix starting at `i` gives these values for all `j` in O(n); alternatively, build a longest-common-prefix table with a DP.
